html:
A Persian mathematician, astronomer and poet, born in Nishapur in 1048, who lived under the Seljuk sultans.

In mathematics he wrote a treatise on algebra that classified cubic equations and solved them using the curves of geometry. Under Sultan Malik-Shah I and his vizier Nizam al-Mulk he worked at an observatory in Isfahan and helped make the Jalali calendar, a solar calendar more accurate than the Julian one then used in Europe.

In the West he is famous as a poet. Quatrains, rubaiyat, about wine, the shortness of life and doubt about the hereafter were attributed to him, though scholars think many are by others. In 1859 Edward FitzGerald published a free English version, the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam, which became one of the most popular poems of the Victorian age. He admired the earlier philosopher Avicenna. He died in Nishapur in 1131.
sum: A Persian mathematician, astronomer and poet, born in Nishapur in 1048, who lived under the Seljuk sultans.
